observations: Actual Google Images shows Hanukkah nine-light lamps, dreidels, coins, latkes, doughnuts, star ornaments and family activities. Do not copy result pixels or layouts.
Plan materially different objects, food preparations, community scenes and paper/felt crafts, with varied character design. Not fifty lamp recolors.
reviewedStructureFacts: Eight Hanukkah lights in one even straight row plus a separate helper light; distinguish the nine-holder Hanukkiah from the seven-branched Temple menorah.
Metadata must not claim a candle is lit, a Hebrew glyph is correct or a religious practice is represented until the actual source is inspected.

headCoveringReview.ownerRequest: Recognizable Jewish Hanukkah celebrants with researched dress and kippot.
facts: Kippah/yarmulke is a small domed head covering, with velvet, knitted and other materials.
Head-covering practice differs among Orthodox, Reform and other communities; no uniform face, hair or skin tone identifies religion.
Traditional long dark coats, hats and sidelocks represent specific communities; do not apply to every person.
Do not use tallit or tefillin as decorative Hanukkah party costume.
